question.value: What is the core mass function (CMF) in the central regions of massive protoclusters (shape, power-law index, presence of a break), and does it differ from the CMF in the G286 protocluster and IRDC clumps measured with the same methods?

evidence.quote: Here we measure the CMF in 28 dense clumps within 3.5 kpc that are likely to be central regions of massive protoclusters, observed via $1.3\:{\rm{mm}}$ dust continuum emission by the ALMAGAL project.
We compare this massive protocluster CMF with those derived using the same methods in the G286 protocluster and a sample of Infrared Dark Clouds.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2019.1.00195.L.

We used the dendrogram algorithm (cite: rosolowsky_structural_2008) as implemented in the python package `astrodendro` to identify cores.
We defined cores as the leaves of the dendrogram.
We required parent structures (trunks) in the dendrogram to have a minimum intensity $F_{\rm min}$ of $4\sigma$.

We also required substructures (*branches* and *leaves*) to have a minimum increase in intensity $\delta$ of $1\sigma$ and a minimum area $S_{\rm{min}}$ of half the synthesized beam to be considered independent entities.

evidence.quote: We note that the effects of using the `clumpfind` algorithm (cite: williams_determining_1994) instead of the dendrogram method were explored in Paper I, and we do not repeat this analysis here.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Herschel dust temperature maps not used due to low resolution

evidence.quote: We note that *Herschel*-derived dust temperature maps have much lower angular resolution ($\gtrsim 30\ensuremath{''}$) than the sizes of the ALMA-identified cores.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pearson χ² statistic considered less powerful than KS/AD

evidence.loc: Single Power-Law Fits to the CMF
evidence.quote: Other distance metrics such as Pearson’s $\chi^{2}$ cumulative test statistic are also potentially applicable for this goal, but have been found to be less powerful than KS or AD based approaches

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Primary-beam-corrected images rejected for core finding

evidence.quote: Attempting to identify cores in primary-beam-corrected images would be compromised as a result of this effect.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Sample yields more than double the cores of previous papers in the series

evidence.quote: As we will see, the sample is large enough that the number of cores identified in the clumps is more than double that of previous samples analyzed in this series of papers.

limitations_admitted.value: No local background correction and no core-scale temperatures

evidence.quote: The core masses we report have significant uncertainties due to no correction being made for the local backgrounds within which the cores are embedded, and also from a lack of temperature information on the scales of the cores.

limitations_admitted.value: True CMF uncertainties underestimated (no f_num uncertainty)

evidence.quote: However, note that these underestimate the true uncertainties, as they do not allow for additional uncertainty in $f_{\rm num}$.
We note that this is not a complete sample of all such massive clumps within 3.5 kpc of the Sun

limitations_admitted.value: Elevated noise in three clumps from cleaning residuals

evidence.quote: We attribute these elevated “noise” estimates to the presence of cleaning residuals, perhaps including effects from real emission features that are just outside the primary beam.

limitations_admitted.value: Small core numbers limit Q analysis

evidence.quote: However, we note that the relatively small sample sizes of cores within each clump severely limit the conclusions that can be derived from these results.

limitations_admitted.value: Binned MLE bias at level Δα ≈ 0.1

evidence.loc: Effects of Dendrogram Parameters, Binning Scheme, and Clump Distance
evidence.quote: The results shown in Table 2 comparing MLE and MLE-B results indicate that these biases are present at a level corresponding to $\Delta\alpha\simeq 0.1$

referee_caveats_inferred: Single dust temperature of 20 K for likely protostellar, internally heated cores could bias high-mass cores upward and flatten the CMF.
Completeness corrections reused from other regions' insertion experiments; large f_num factors (≳20) at low masses dominate the true CMF and the break location.
Varying linear resolution across 0.76-3.5 kpc mixes core definitions; break scale may be resolution-dependent (authors note this).
No imaging or beam information reported, so S_min and flux integration cannot be checked.
Double PPL vs single PL comparison relies on WLS fits to ~7-13 bins, so AICc weights are sensitive to binning.

missing_for_reproduction: Continuum imaging recipe and per-clump beam sizes
Tabulated f_flux and f_num correction curves
Exact continuum frequency used for mass conversion
Analysis code for bootstrap, PPL/AICc fits and LOWESS
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: 28 single-pointing 12m continuum images are small (<1 GB); re-imaging from calibrated ALMAGAL measurement sets would likely require tens to hundreds of GB.
reproducibility.score_reason: Core catalog (Table 4) and statistical recipe are detailed, but imaging/calibration are unstated and the incompleteness corrections are only shown graphically.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data from an ALMA large program in the archive; core catalog with raw and flux-corrected masses allows the MLE fits, M_min selection and KS comparisons to be redone numerically, though true-CMF corrections require Fig. 2 curves.

methods_papers.why: MLE power-law fitting, KS M_min selection, bootstrap p-values

Paper II: IRDC clump CMF, same methods
